Sea surface dissolved oxygen validation using gridded observations from ZISSOU¶

Matchup procedure: The model and observations were matched up as follows. First, the model dataset was cropped by a small amount to make sure cells close to the boundary were removed. The model was then regridded to the observational grid using bilinear remmaping. Only grid cells with model and observational data were maintained. The following model output was used to compare with the observational values: o2.

Baseline climatologies of sea surface dissolved oxygen¶

Climatologies of model and observational sea surface dissolved oxygen are shown in the figures below. The model climatology is calculated using the years 2000-2004.

Figure 1: Annual average surface dissolved oxygen from the model (2000-2004) and observations. Data is limited to the 2nd and 98th percentile of the combined model and observational data. Arrows indicate that values can exceed the colorbar limits.

Assessing model bias for surface dissolved oxygen¶

Figure 2 shows the average bias of surface dissolved oxygen simulated by the model. A positive bias indicates that the model overestimates the observation, while a negative bias indicates that the model overpredicts the observation.

The spatial average bias of surface dissolved oxygen is 6.08 mmol m-3. Overall, the model overestimates the observations in 89.6% of the model domain.

Figure 2: Bias of surface dissolved oxygen from the model. A positive bias indicates that the model overestimates the observation. For clarity, the colorbar is limited to the 2nd and 98th percentile of the data.

Can the model reproduce seasonality of sea surface dissolved oxygen concentration?¶

The ability of the model to reproduce seasonality of sea surface dissolved oxygen was assessed by comparing the modelled and observed seasonal cycle of dissolved oxygen. First, we derive a monthly climatology for the model data. Then, we calculate the Pearson correlation coefficient between the modelled and observed dissolved oxygen at each grid cell.

Note: we are only assessing the ability of the model to reproduce the ability of the model to reproduce seasonal changes, not long-term trends.

Figure 3: Seasonal temporal correlation between model and observations for surface dissolved oxygen. This is the Pearson correlation coefficient between climatological monthly mean values in the model and observations.

The seasonal cycles of simulated and observed dissolved oxygen are compared in Figure 4 below. This figure shows the model and observation average in each month of the year, and the differences between the two each month

Figure 4: Monthly mean surface dissolved oxygen for the model, observation and the difference between model and observations. For clarity, the maximum values are capped to the 98th percentiles. Arrows on the colorbars indicate values beyond the colorbar limits.

Can the model reproduce spatial patterns of sea surface dissolved oxygen concentration?¶

The ability of the model to reproduce spatial patterns of sea surface dissolved oxygen was assessed by comparing the modelled and observed dissolved oxygen at each grid cell. We calculated the Pearson correlation coefficient between the modelled and observed dissolved oxygen at each grid cell.

This was carried out monthly and using the annual mean in each grid cell

Regional assessment of model performance for sea surface dissolved oxygen concentration¶

We assessed the regional performance of the model by comparing the model with observations in a number of regions. The regions considered are mapped below.

Figure 5: Regions used for validation of sea surface dissolved oxygen concentration.

Time series were constructed comparing the monthly mean of the spatial average sea surface dissolved oxygen in each region. The spatial average was calculated using the mean of all grid cells within each region, accounting for grid cell area.

Figure 6: Seasonal cycle of sea surface dissolved oxygen concentration for model and observations for each region. The spatial average is taken over the region.

The table below shows the average bias of sea surface dissolved oxygen in each region. The bias is calculated as the modelled value minus the observed value. A positive bias indicates that the model overestimates the observed value, while a negative bias indicates that the model underestimates the observed value.

The bias (mmol m-3) column represents the spatial average of the annual mean modelled value minus the observed value.
